main_text.l: August.de verb.Apost.Serm.18. Duo sunt ha-bitacula: unum in igne æterno, alterum in regno a-terno.
Chrysostom.in Matth.8.hom.19. Justorum anima in manu Dei sunt: peccatorum vero post exitum continuo abducuntur, quod è Lazaro & divite planum est, &c.
Resp. A posse ad esse non valet: non vult. Habent Mosen & prophetas, &c.
Resp. Mentiuntur, ut stabiliant νεκυομαντεία[?], & fabulam purgatorii.
Obiectio 111. Animæ Mosis & Eliæ apparue-runt, Matt.17.
Resp. Exemplum singulare & dissimile non fa-cit regulam.
Resp. Fuit spectrum diabolicum, specie Sa-muelis indutum, ut stabiliretur magia. 2. Cor. 11. 14. Satan transformans se in angelum lucis.
Conclusio: Vana igitur opinio gentilium, ani-mos improborum, vel inhumatorum, vel violenta morte decedentium ad sepulcra mutari in dæmones errantes.
Et Monachorum: Spectra esse animas defun-ctorum è cœlo, vel inferno, vel purgatorio rede-ntes.
Antithefis: Esse vel inanes umbras, vel ludibria impostorum & Satanæ: vel ipsos dæmones, specie humana vestitos.

page.notes: Show-through from the facing page appears at the right edge and was left out. The first line is flush left and may continue from the previous page, so cont="true" is a guess. The Greek word after "ut stabiliant" is only partly legible and is marked [?]. "rede-ntes" is as far as the hyphenated word is legible; "u" is uncertain. The "S" in "August." and the ligature in "August." are read as st. The line-end hyphens are printed and kept.
